issue.title: test_header_resolver_late_read_does_not_poison_leak_snapshot fails on sibling xdist temp leftovers
issue.description:
The nested pytest for this node passed both inner tests (2 passed in 2.37s) during `sase tool run check` run `07efa9e8ef7c8b771f7451912f203341`. The outer node then failed `assert result.ret == 0` because the suite temp-leak guard saw a sibling xdist worker leftover:

```
The test suite left new entries in a watched temp directory:
  /var/tmp/sase-cf079551 (1 new):
    - release-watch-abandon-ghbvnu2a
```

That `release-watch-abandon-*` directory is not produced by the header-worker tests this node runs. The nested subprocess inherits the parent suite's watched temp root, so another worker's unmanaged temp entry fails this node even when its own tests are green.

Isolated rerun on the same tree: 1 passed in 9.02s.

Not a duplicate of sase-1vl (60s nested-pytest timeouts on different nodes) or sase-t6 (thread-count snapshot on a different node). Same file and loaded-lane nested-pytest class; related, different mechanism.

The recovery-claims split that triggered this check did not touch leak-detector or header-worker code.

task_type_fields.evidence: 1 loaded-lane fail in ToolRun 07efa9e8ef7c8b771f7451912f203341 (inner 2 passed, outer ret!=0 from temp-leak guard seeing release-watch-abandon-*); 1/1 isolated pass on the same tree. Not reproduced serially.
task_type_fields.repro_cmd: sase tool run check (scoped xdist lane); isolated: .venv/bin/pytest tests/test_global_state_leak_detector.py::test_header_resolver_late_read_does_not_poison_leak_snapshot -q

issue.creation_reason: A scoped check of an unrelated recovery-claims split failed this node under xdist load; the inner tests passed and an isolated rerun passed, so this is a loaded-lane flake.
